info.title: Aperture API
info.description: Aperture's HTTP API. This schema is the single source of truth for the frontend's types: it generates packages/api-client, which is never hand-edited.

post.description: Answer a call. Membership and blocks are re-checked here rather than trusted from the invite.
Start a call in a conversation. Returns ICE servers for every call and a LiveKit room token for group calls, and rings the other participants over their socket.

get.description: Liveness and dependency check. Verifies Postgres, Redis and object storage by performing real operations against each.
One media row, including its processing state.

patch.description: Set alt text. May be empty — the field is always present, but never required.

delete.description: Soft delete. A scheduled job removes the objects later.

post.description: Signal that the browser finished its PUT. Enqueues validation and derivative generation. Poll the detail endpoint until state leaves 'pending'.
Reserve a media row and return a presigned URL to PUT the file to. The row is created in state=pending; the bytes go straight to object storage and never through this server.

get.description: Conversations you are in, most recently active first.

post.description: Start a DM or a group. A DM between two people is unique.

get.description: A window of a conversation, addressed by seq.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return everything with a higher seq. This is the whole offline-sync story: 'send me everything after 4821'.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Scrollback: return messages older than this seq.

post.description: Send a message. Idempotent on client_id: retrying after a timeout returns the message that already exists rather than creating a second one.
Move your read position forward. Never backward.
Report a post, comment, user or piece of media. Idempotent per reporter per subject: reporting twice returns the first report.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Snowflake id of the last item on the previous page. Ids are time-ordered, so this is simply 'older than that one'.

post.description: Comment on a post, or reply to a comment.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Snowflake id of the last item on the previous page. Ids are time-ordered, so this is simply 'older than that one'.

post.description: Publish a post from media that has finished processing.

get.description: Recent public posts from accounts you do not follow.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Snowflake id of the last item on the previous page. Ids are time-ordered, so this is simply 'older than that one'.

get.description: Posts from accounts you follow, newest first.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Snowflake id of the last item on the previous page. Ids are time-ordered, so this is simply 'older than that one'.

post.description: Mint a short-lived signed ticket for the socket gateway. The gateway verifies it locally and never calls back.

get.description: One account's public profile, with its counts.

post.description: Block an account, severing follows both ways.

delete.description: Unblock. Does not restore the follows that blocking severed.

post.description: Follow, or request to follow a private account.

delete.description: Unfollow, or withdraw a pending request.

post.description: Approve or decline a pending follow request.

delete.description: Delete your account. Content disappears from every read path immediately; the rows are erased permanently after a grace period.

post.description: Mail a password reset link. Answers 204 whether or not the address is known.
Complete a password reset and sign every session out.
Create an account. Signs the new account in.

get.description: Pending follow requests for your account.
Find accounts by username or display name.

post.description: Sign in with email and password.

Call.description: Everything a client needs to join a call and nothing it does not.

Conversation.description: A conversation as it appears in the inbox.

CreatePostRequest.description: Publishing a post from media that is already uploaded and processed.

CurrentUser.description: The signed-in user seeing their own account. Adds the private bits.

username.description: Case-insensitively unique. Shown in metadata position.

is_private.description: Private accounts turn follows into requests pending approval.

FollowRequest.description: A pending request, from the perspective of the account being asked.

FollowState.description: What the follow button should read after acting.

IceServer.description:
One `RTCIceServer`, handed to the browser verbatim.

`credential` is a TURN password that expires — see `core/turn.py`. It is
not a secret worth protecting for long, which is exactly why it is safe to
send here at all.

JoinCallRequest.description:
Answering an invite.

`call_id` and `mode` come back from the invite the callee received over
the socket. Neither is trusted for authorization — `join_call` re-checks
membership and blocks against the conversation before minting anything.

LoginRequest.description: Credentials. Email is the login identifier here, not username.

Media.description:
A media row as the client sees it.

Everything the develop-in needs is here: `blurhash` for the canvas,
`width`/`height` to reserve the space so nothing shifts, and
`dominant_color` for the ambient glow.

alt_text.description: May be empty, but the composer always presents the field.

MediaSource.description: One rendition of an image, for a `srcset`.

MessagePage.description: A window of a conversation, addressed by `seq` rather than by offset.

PasswordResetConfirmRequest.description:
Complete a reset.

`uid` and `token` come straight back out of the link, so they are opaque
strings here — validating their shape would only move the same rejection
earlier and give a probe a way to tell malformed from wrong.

PasswordResetRequestRequest.description: Ask for a link. An address, and nothing else.

PatchedAltTextRequest.description: Alt text may be empty, but the field is always present.

Post.description: A post as the feed and the contact sheet see it.

PostPage.description:
A cursor-paginated page of posts.

`next_cursor` is the id of the last post on the page, or null at the end.
No total count: producing one means a `COUNT(*)` over the whole feed, and
nothing in the UI shows it.

Profile.description:
A profile header.

Counts come from the `counters` app, never from a `COUNT(*)` — a follower
count on a popular account is a sequential scan over millions of rows, and
it renders on every profile view.

`follow_state` is what the button reads: absent, `pending` while a private
account considers the request, or `accepted`.

RealtimeTicket.description: A short-lived credential for the socket gateway.

ReasonEnum.description:
* `csam` - Child sexual abuse material
* `violence` - Violence or threats
* `harassment` - Harassment or bullying
* `hate` - Hate speech
* `nudity` - Adult nudity or sexual activity
* `spam` - Spam or scam
* `self_harm` - Self-harm or suicide
* `copyright` - Copyright or trademark
* `other` - Something else

RegisterRequest.description:
What it takes to open an account.

`username` is constrained here rather than only at the database, because
the model's uniqueness will not tell you that a space is not allowed. The
pattern matches what a profile URL can carry — `/u/<username>` — so a name
that cannot be linked to cannot be chosen.

Report.description:
A report, as the person who filed it may see it.

Deliberately thin: the reporter learns that their report exists and
nothing about what happened next. Telling them the outcome would tell them
whether the person they reported was actioned, which is a privacy leak
about a third party and, when the reporter is the harasser, a feedback
signal for tuning the next attempt.

SendMessageRequest.description:
What the client sends.

`client_id` is required and minted by the browser. It is the only thing
standing between a flaky network and a duplicated message, so there is no
server-side default — a client that does not send one does not get
idempotency, and should be made to notice.

UploadIntentRequestRequest.description: What the client asks for before it uploads anything.

UploadIntentResponse.description: The reservation, and the URL to PUT to.

User.description: A user as anyone may see them. No email, no permission flags.

username.description: Case-insensitively unique. Shown in metadata position.

is_private.description: Private accounts turn follows into requests pending approval.
